issue: Does the First Amendment require a reasonable mistake-of-age defense to a charge of producing child pornography under 18 U.S.C. § 2251(a)?

sides.position: The First Amendment requires that a defendant be allowed to present a reasonable mistake-of-age defense to a § 2251 charge.
cases: United States v. U.S. District Court for the Central District of California, 858 F.2d 534 (9th Cir. 1988)

sides.position: The First Amendment does not require a reasonable mistake-of-age defense to charges of producing child pornography under § 2251(a).
cases: United States v. Wilson, 565 F.3d 1059 (8th Cir. 2008)
United States v. Thurber, 106 F.4th 814 (8th Cir. 2024)

this_court: does not require a reasonable mistake-of-age defense under the First Amendment, following Wilson and rejecting the Ninth Circuit's contrary holding
quote: [o]ther circuits have split as to whether the First Amendment requires reading a reasonable-mistake-of-age defense into [§ 2251]
cite: United States v. Norman Thurber, 106 F.4th 814 (8th Cir. 2024)
